29a4b08c4b3b808d260f985a7f4d489797ad5ce8: A resort on a human scale, Brand – Brandnertal prides itself on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than impressive figures. Its 47.6 km of runs are ideal for a stay of 3 to 4 days, especially for families or skiers who don't need to constantly change their playground. Brand – Brandnertal's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, a well-organised childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Brand – Brandnertal's altitude (904 m at the base, 2,000 m at the top) allows it to maintain decent snow cover through the depths of winter. January and February are the most reliable; in December and March, it is best to check conditions before finalising a booking. The budget for a stay in Brand – Brandnertal is clearly high: €66 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence — but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Brand – Brandnertal does not rival the giants of skiing, and does not pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underestimated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

29cf72c699dffa6932b85b75d5c87ee7c97ed63e: Breuil-Cervinia is one of the rare resorts offering more than 322 km of runs — a colossal ski area that even the fastest skiers would not cover in a week. With 51 lifts and 0 runs listed, it is a destination that can absorb all visitor flows without ever feeling crowded. Breuil-Cervinia has kept the identity of an authentic mountain village, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for the clean air, the unspoilt scenery and a friendly atmosphere that stands in contrast to the industrialisation of skiing in some large ski areas. As for snow cover, Breuil-Cervinia is in a strong position with its summit at 3899 m — even in capricious winters, the upper runs hold up well until April. The village at 2050 m is also well placed to offer comfortable conditions from mid-December onwards. The budget for a stay in Breuil-Cervinia is clearly high: €123 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and high-altitude restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence — but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Breuil-Cervinia lives up to its promises. A Northern Alps resort that will suit most profiles without disappointing.
